verdict: Boxed orange juice wins slightly because it has fewer calories. But both are sugar in liquid form, so how often you drink them matters more than which one you pick.
why: 1 box of orange juice (250 ml) is an estimated ~110 kcal. 1 can of soft drink (325 ml) is ~140 kcal. A difference of about 30 kcal.
Orange juice has a little protein (2 g), soft drinks 0 g. Neither helps much in keeping you full.
Calories from sweet drinks slip in easily without you feeling it. You finish it in 5 minutes, but your stomach doesn't feel like you just ate.
A 325 ml can is bigger than a 250 ml box. Once a can is opened, you usually finish it.
when_a: Orange juice is okay once in a while, for example when you have no time for breakfast and want something light while you look for food.
when_b: A soft drink can fit during a weekend lepak or a BBQ with friends. One can, enjoyed slowly.
tip: Pour half into a glass full of ice, and keep the other half for the afternoon. You still get the taste, and the calories are split in two.

faq.q: Is boxed orange juice the same as eating an orange?
faq.a: Not the same. A whole orange has fibre that keeps you full longer. Boxed juice is easier to drink a lot of without feeling full.

faq.q: If I still want a fizzy drink, is there a lighter option?
faq.a: Plain soda water with a squeeze of lime is an almost zero-calorie option. If you want something sweet, choose a small size and don't make it a daily habit.
